body:
If this issue effects common system configurations aside from FreeBSD, I think it would be a worthwhile fix.

``` c
tempfile.c
 85 /// Get the name of temp directory. This directory would be created on the first                                                                                                                        
 86 /// call to this function.                                                                                                                                                                              
 87 char_u *vim_gettempdir(void)                                                                                                                                                                            
 88 {                                                                                                                                                                                                       
 89   if (vim_tempdir == NULL) {                                                                                                                                                                            
 90     vim_maketempdir();                                                                                                                                                                                  
 91   }                                                                                                                                                                                                     
 92                                                                                                                                                                                                         
 93   return vim_tempdir;                                                                                                                                                                                   
 94 }
```

At first glance, this could be fixed by modifying the check on line 89 to additionally check if the directory exists.

When @Hinidu encountered this he recognized it as a performance choice, IIRC. In what scenarios would the directory be deleted? It may be that we only need to do a sanity check at certain times, but hopefully not every time.

issue.title: Unit test tempfile - add more test cases

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
The two commits in this PR originates as a followup to issue #1432. I wanted to add a test case or two to detect the issue. In the act of doing this, I realize a few more test cases of a similar nature could be added. Also, I added a test to directly verify temp directory deletion.

The new test cases are mostly concerned with testing two successive calls of gettempdir or tempname, and when the calls are interrupted by deleting the temp directory, or by doing the other operation. For example,
1. gettempdir, gettempdir
2. gettempdir, deltempdir, gettempdir - 'internally' delete temp directory
3. gettempdir, lfs.rmdir, gettempdir - 'externally' delete temp directory
4. gettempdir, tempname, gettempdir

Test case 1 appears in the original unit test, which is a check for idempotency.
Test case 4 checks for any side effects between gettempdir and tempname.
Test case 3 checks for #1432 and is to be compared with test case 2. Test case 3 is written to succeed, although it should more naturally fail, if it wasn't for the performance hit that will occur (see comments in #1432).

A similar test sequence is repeated for tempname.

Roughly speaking, the first commit re-expresses the original unit test with shortcut aliases so there is less verbosity. The first commit also merges two of the test cases into one. The second commit adds the extra test cases.

issue.title: feat: try to recover from missing tempdir

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
Continues https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/11284


## Problem:
If vim_tempdir mysteriously goes missing (likely by "antivirus" on Windows), any plugins using tempname() will be broken for the rest of the session. #1432 #9833
https://groups.google.com/g/vim_use/c/ef55jNm5czI

### Steps:

    mkdir foo
    TMPDIR=./foo nvim
    :echo tempname()
    !rm -r foo
    :echo tempname()
    tempname() still uses the foo path even though it was deleted.

## Solution:

- Don't assume that vim_tempdir exists.
- If it goes missing, create a new one, and log a WARN message.
- If it goes missing again, create a new one and show an error.

Rejected in Vim for performance reasons:
https://groups.google.com/g/vim_use/c/qgRob9SWDv8/m/FAOFVVcDTv0J
https://groups.google.com/g/vim_dev/c/cogp-Vye4oo/m/d_SVFXBbnnoJ

Testing shows that `vim_gettempdir` is not called frequently.

Fixes #1432
Fixes #9833
Fixes #11250
Related: stdpath("run") f50135a32e11c535e1dc3a8e9460c5b4e640ee86
